subject: history
title: Causes of War: Cause Analysis
welcome_lead: Today you'll sort long-term causes from short-term triggers and rank what mattered most.
meta_desc: GCSE History Causes of War cause analysis — long-term and short-term causes of WWI and WWII.
final_note: You can now separate long-term causes from triggers and explain how they linked together.

concepts.def: A deep reason building up over years
Events in the months before war
Germany's 1914 plan to beat France fast then Russia
1938 deal letting Hitler take the Sudetenland
1939 secret deal between Hitler and Stalin

walkthroughs.body_html:
Long-term causes built up tension for decades.

The Anglo-German naval race, rival empires in Africa, the Balkan crises and the rigid alliance system all primed Europe for war well before 1914.

Austria-Hungary blamed Serbia for the assassination and issued a tough ultimatum.

Russia mobilised to defend Serbia. Germany declared war on Russia and France, then attacked through Belgium using the Schlieffen Plan. Britain joined to defend Belgium on 4 August 1914.

The Treaty of Versailles blamed Germany, took land, limited its army and demanded reparations.

In the 1930s Hitler broke its terms one by one. The Munich Agreement (1938) and the Nazi-Soviet Pact (1939) cleared his path to invade Poland.

mcqs.q: Which is a LONG-term cause of WWI?
options: Sarajevo assassination
Russian mobilisation
Anglo-German naval race
German invasion of Belgium

mcqs.q: What did the 1938 Munich Agreement give Hitler?
options: Austria
The Sudetenland
Poland
The Rhineland

mcqs.q: Why did the League of Nations fail to prevent WWII?
options: Hitler called off the attack to invade the USSR immediately.
The League failed because Hitler banned it in 1933.
The League failed because no countries joined it.
Absence of the US, requirement of unanimous decisions, no armed force of its own, weak responses to Manchuria (1931) and Abyssinia (1935), and great-power self-interest.

mcqs.q: What caused the First World War?
options: The League failed because Hitler banned it in 1933.
Germany declared war on Britain to seize colonies.
The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand caused the war.
Long-term tensions (militarism, alliances, imperialism, nationalism) combined with the July Crisis triggered by the assassination of Franz Ferdinand.

mcqs.q: Why did Britain win the Battle of Britain?
options: The RAF won because Spitfires were better than any German aircraft.
The League failed because Hitler banned it in 1933.
Hitler called off the attack to invade the USSR immediately.
Radar, the Dowding command system, home advantage in pilot recovery, German tactical errors (switching to bombing cities), and adequate fighter production.
